_comment: Nodes whose executor returns a flow port their contract does not declare. Recorded at PHASE 9 recovery item 6 with 45 entries; item 7 classified all 45 and reduced them to 1. The 44 fixed were the same bug the save/load nodes had -- the executor returned the unprefixed spelling (success / touched / next) while the declaration used exec_*, so every pin the editor offered the author was unreachable. Assets settled the direction: 43 of the 45 nodes appear in no .zlogic at all, no alias covered the unprefixed spelling and no test asserted it, while the declarations are hand-authored with localised labels. The gate in tools/audit_node_system.py fails on any NEW entry, on any entry left here after it is fixed, and on any entry whose ports changed. This is a debt with a name and a bound, not an exemption.
_provenance: PHASE 9 recovery item 7, regenerated from tools/audit_node_system.py:executor_output_violations(). 0 assets were modified.

_reasons.set_variable: Out of scope by item 7 section 15: set_variable has two executors (misc_nodes and scene_nodes) and the scene_nodes one -- which wins by load order -- returns ['done', 'next']. Only 'next' is declared, and 10 asset instances wire 8 flow edges to it. Untangling 'done' means choosing a side in the duplicate-executor conflict, which item 7 is forbidden to touch. Item 7 additionally found that _EXPLICIT_PORT_CONTRACTS shadows the declarative definition here: the legacy table declares 'next' while misc_nodes declares 'exec_done'. Both facts belong to the set_variable duplicate item.
